mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep falling from their current lows, weekday downtown foot traffic will keep shrinking and RETAIL_REC will remain below its prior four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay at or below their current weekly averages for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL together with weak TRANSIT means more time spent at home and fewer discretionary shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should fall further within the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +2 while TRANSIT stays below -10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next 7 days after RESIDENTIAL is above +2 and TRANSIT remains below -10.

mechanism_narrative: When transit mobility drops abruptly, access frictions and perceived closure risk reduce shopping visits with a short lag, so RETAIL_REC should be lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall within 14 days of a weekly TRANSIT drop of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a prior week of weakness signals more outdoor activity and spillover spending on nearby retail, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns from negative weekly change to positive weekly change
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days after PARKS reverses from negative to positive weekly change.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while RETAIL_REC stays depressed, households are substituting toward essential trips and away from discretionary shopping, which should keep RETAIL_REC weak over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above +5 and RETAIL_REC is below -5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above +5 and RETAIL_REC staying below -5 at the trigger date.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT imply reduced commuting intensity and fewer retail opportunities, so retail mobility should continue falling over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below their current weekly levels.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in PARKS with only modest change in other categories signals weather or seasonal conditions that suppress outdoor movement and carry over to less retail browsing, reducing RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below 0 for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next 7 days after PARKS remains negative for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rises while GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both weaken, people are concentrating at home and making fewer combined errand-and-shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should stay below its recent mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT stay weak.
